subject: Vocabulary
topic: Antonyms — SSC CGL Level Word Pairs (W10)

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to: ABUNDANT
questions.explanation: B is correct. ABUNDANT = existing or available in large quantities. Its antonym is SCARCE = deficient in quantity, hard to find. Trap: 'Plentiful' and 'Excessive' are synonyms of Abundant; 'Sufficient' means just enough — not the direct opposite of large quantities.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to: VICTORY
questions.explanation: B is correct. VICTORY = winning, success in a contest. Its direct antonym is DEFEAT = failure, being beaten. Trap: 'Triumph' and 'Success' are synonyms of Victory; 'Achievement' is a broader positive accomplishment — not the opposite of winning a contest.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to: ELOQUENT
questions.explanation: C is correct. ELOQUENT = fluent, persuasive, and powerfully expressive in speech. INARTICULATE = unable to express thoughts clearly in words — the direct opposite. Trap: 'Articulate' and 'Fluent' are synonyms of Eloquent; 'Verbose' means using too many words (wordy), which is the opposite in style but not meaning.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to: BENEVOLENT
questions.explanation: C is correct. BENEVOLENT = well-wishing, kind, and generous in spirit (bene = well + vole = wish). MALEVOLENT = having or showing a wish to do evil (male = ill + vole = wish) — a perfect antonym by Latin prefix reversal. Trap: 'Kind', 'Generous', and 'Charitable' are all synonyms of Benevolent.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to: TRANSIENT
questions.explanation: D is correct. TRANSIENT = passing away quickly, not lasting (from Latin transire = to pass over). Its antonym is PERMANENT = lasting or intended to last indefinitely. Trap: 'Brief', 'Temporary', and 'Fleeting' are all synonyms of Transient — this is a classic SSC trap where three similar words are offered as distractors.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to: LETHARGY
questions.explanation: C is correct. LETHARGY = a lack of energy and enthusiasm, sluggishness. VIGOUR = physical and mental energy, strength, and activeness — the direct antonym. Trap: 'Laziness', 'Sloth', and 'Apathy' (lack of enthusiasm) are all synonymous with Lethargy, not antonymous.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to: OBSEQUIOUS
questions.explanation: C is correct. OBSEQUIOUS = excessively submissive and eager to please, fawning and cringing. Its antonym is ASSERTIVE = confident, self-assured, and willing to defend one's own rights and views directly. Trap: 'Servile', 'Sycophantic', and 'Flattering' are all synonyms of Obsequious. Knowing 'obsequious' is essential — it appears in SSC CGL comprehension and antonym questions.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to: LOQUACIOUS
questions.explanation: D is correct. LOQUACIOUS = very talkative, fond of talking at length. TACITURN = habitually silent and reserved, saying little — the precise antonym. Trap: 'Talkative', 'Garrulous' (excessively talkative), and 'Verbose' (using too many words) are all synonyms of Loquacious. Students who don't know 'taciturn' often pick 'verbose' by elimination error.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to: EPHEMERAL
questions.explanation: D is correct. EPHEMERAL = lasting for a very short time, momentary (from Greek ephemeros = lasting only a day). EVERLASTING = lasting forever, eternal — its antonym. Trap: 'Temporary', 'Brief', and 'Transient' are all synonyms of Ephemeral. The pattern of three synonyms as distractors is a classic SSC format that rewards knowing the target word.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to: AUDACIOUS
questions.explanation: C is correct. AUDACIOUS = showing willingness to take bold risks; daring, brave, and sometimes recklessly so. TIMID = lacking courage, easily frightened, shrinking from bold action — the direct antonym. Trap: 'Brave', 'Bold', and 'Daring' are all synonyms of Audacious. Students must recognise that TIMID is the only contrasting option.
